summary: Count to 100 by ones and tens and recognize the count as a growing pattern.
Count to 120 from any number, noticing growing and repeating patterns; read, write, and match numerals.
Build and break apart tens and ones in several ways, such as 20 as 1 ten and 10 ones.
Build and break apart hundreds, tens, and ones in several ways, such as 207 as 20 tens 7 ones.
Count within 1000 and skip-count by 2s, 5s, 10s, and 100s; explain the patterns (adds 2s).
Tell and write time to the nearest five minutes on analog and digital clocks; a.m./p.m. moves to grade 3.
Recognize coins and bills and know what each is worth.
Tell time to the nearest minute using a.m. and p.m., measure time intervals, and solve elapsed-time problems.
Fluently add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers with any efficient algorithm, such as partial sums.
Show fraction measurements (halves, fourths, eighths) in a line plot, bar graph, or pictograph and solve problems.
Draw and identify points, lines, rays, angles (including straight and reflex), and parallel and perpendicular lines.
Classify shapes by lines and angle types; sort triangles by angles and by sides (scalene, isosceles, equilateral).
Use parentheses in numerical expressions and evaluate them; brackets and braces dropped.
Fluently multiply multi-digit whole numbers with an efficient algorithm, such as partial products or the standard one.
Show fraction measurements to sixteenths in line plots, bar graphs, or pictographs; solve problems with them.
